newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yeltsin signs decree cutting gas tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yeltsin signs decree cutting gas tariffs.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree on lowering natural gas tariffs for domestic users, the presidential press service said on Thursday.
"The President has signed the decree 'On Lowering Gas Prices for Russian Users,'" the press service said in a statement. It said details of the text would be released separately.

Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov was quoted by Interfax news agency on Wednesday as saying wholesale prices for gas supplied by the Gazprom monopoly to domestic industrial users would be cut by 40 percent.

But it quoted Nemtsov, who is also first deputy prime minister, as saying on Thursday that tariffs would be cut by up to 40 percent and would only apply to industrial gas users who pay off their debts to the budget by the end of 1997. It was not immediately clear when the rate cuts would be enacted.
The rate cuts are part of a wider campaign by Moscow to reign in its biggest debtors, including Gazprom, to solve its budget shortfall crisis.

The press service statement also said Gazprom was completing work on paying off debts to the government. Gazprom said on Wednesday it still owed about 3.5 trillion roubles ($608 million) to the government.
